final_candidates.decision_summary: R157 is in the catalytic FAD-binding domain and R157Q is a known severe MTHFR-deficiency variant causing markedly reduced enzyme activity, best matching the goal of abolishing activity.
A222V (C677T) is the classic thermolabile variant causing substantial activity loss via reduced FAD binding; WT residue A222 verified in the catalytic region, though abolition may be partial.

stop_reason.detail: Self-review converged and no evidence tools are available, so additional iteration would not improve the Top-3.

history.rationale: The common A222V (C677T) variant is known to produce a thermolabile enzyme with substantially reduced activity, indicating the region is sensitive; it is a validated loss-of-function direction.
A222V (C677T) is a well-characterized variant causing thermolability and ~65% activity loss, though rarely complete abolition.
Arg157 is a recurrent severe pathogenic variant in MTHFR deficiency patients, suggesting it plays a key structural or catalytic role; mutation to Gln removes a critical positive charge.
R157 is in the catalytic FAD-binding domain and R157Q is a known severe MTHFR deficiency variant with markedly reduced activity.
E429A corresponds to the common A1298C polymorphism in the regulatory domain, which reduces activity and is well tolerated structurally; adding as a third documented LOF-leaning variant.
